newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: New fraud discovered at Argentine customs - paper.
newsitem.headline: New fraud discovered at Argentine customs - paper.

text.p: Argentina's customs service, long plagued by graft and contraband scandals, may have lost $200 million in revenues due to alleged fraud by fishing companies, Clarin daily newspaper reported Monday.
An internal investigation revealed that 19 companies operating in Southern Argentina received $200 million in tax reimbursements from alleged squid exports between 1992-1995.
But during the same period those firms declared only $5 million in exports for tax purposes, Clarin said.
No one was immediately available at the customs service for comment.
Until recently, fishing firms operating in Patagonian waters qualified for tax deductions on their exports.

The Clarin report was the latest in a series of scandals at Argentina's customs service. According to the government, some $10 billion worth of goods entered the capital's port illegally between 1993-1996, costing the state $3 billion in lost tariffs.

In December, authorities arrested six people and launched a search for many others after discovering 40 tonnes of cameras, surgical instruments, perfume and other goods had been smuggled in from the United States.

Also in December, legislators discovered 1.5 tonnes of cocaine in safe deposit boxes the service had rented at state-run Banco Nacion. The drugs, with a street value of $150 million, should have been burned five days after seizure, but some had been there in bags and suitcases since 1984.
